tests.description: MULTIPLE SOCKET-OUTLETS integral with ME EQUIPMENT complied with 16.2 d), second dash; and 16.9.2
MAINS PLUG not fitted with more than one POWER SUPPLY CORD

POWER SUPPLY CORDS are no less robust than ordinary tough rubber sheathed flexible cord (IEC 60245-1:2003, Annex A, designation 53) or ordinary polyvinyl chloride sheathed flexible cord (IEC 60227-1:1993, Annex A, design. 53)
Only polyvinyl chloride insulated POWER SUPPLY CORD with appropriate temperature rating used for ME EQUIPMENT having external metal parts with a temperature > 75°C touchable by the cord in NORMAL USE
NOMINAL cross-sectional area of conductors of POWER SUPPLY CORDS of ME EQUIPMENT is not less than in Table 17 (mm2 Cu)
APPLIANCE COUPLERS complying with IEC 60320-1 are considered to comply with 8.11.3.5 and 8.11.3.6
Cord anchorage (for APPLIANCE COUPLERS not complying with IEC 60320-1) - multiple sub-requirements a) through f)

sub_requirements.description: Conductors of POWER SUPPLY CORD provided with strain relief and insulation protected from abrasion at point of entry to ME EQUIPMENT or a MAINS CONNECTOR by a cord anchorage

Cord anchorage of POWER SUPPLY CORD is made of and arranged as specified when a total insulation failure of POWER SUPPLY CORD caused conductive non-PROTECTIVELY EARTHED ACCESSIBLE PARTS to exceed limits of 8.4 (insulating material; or metal insulated from conductive ACCESSIBLE PARTS non-PROTECTIVELY EARTHED by a MEANS OF PROTECTION; or metal provided with an insulating lining affixed to cord anchorage)
Cord anchorage prevents cord from being clamped by a screw bearing directly on cord insulation
Screws to be operated when replacing POWER SUPPLY CORD do not serve to secure any components other than parts of cord anchorage
Conductors of POWER SUPPLY CORD arranged to prevent PROTECTIVE EARTH CONDUCTOR against strain as long as phase conductors are in contact with their terminals when cord anchorage fails
Cord anchorage prevents POWER SUPPLY CORD from being pushed into ME EQUIPMENT or MAINS CONNECTOR

tests.description: Pull test: Conductors of POWER SUPPLY CORD disconnected from terminals or from MAINS CONNECTOR and cord subjected 25 times to a pull applied with no jerks, each time for 1 s, on sheath of the value in Table 18
Torque test: Cord subjected to a torque in Table 18 for 1 min immediately after pull tests
Cord anchorage did not allow cord sheath to be longitudinally displaced by more than 2 mm or conductor ends to move over a distance of more than 1 mm from their connected position
CREEPAGE and CLEARANCES not reduced below limits in 8.9
It was not possible to push the cord into ME EQUIPMENT or MAINS CONNECTOR to an extent the cord or internal parts would be damaged
POWER SUPPLY CORDS other than for STATIONARY ME EQUIPMENT protected against excessive bending at inlet opening by means of an insulating cord guard or appropriately shaped opening

Cord guard complied with test of IEC 60335-1:2001, Clause 25.14; or ME EQUIPMENT placed such that axis of cord guard projected at an angle of 45° with cord free from stress, and a mass equal 10 x D2 gram attached to the free end of cord

semantic_fragments.content: A clear warning notice is marked on outside of ME EQUIPMENT to indicate it exceeds allowable touch voltage (symbol 10 of Table D.1 is insufficient). For a part that could not be disconnected from supply by an external switch or a plug device accessible at all times, the required cover or warning notice complied with this clause. Standard test finger of Fig 6 applied.

Cord anchorage sub-requirement b) specifies that when total insulation failure of POWER SUPPLY CORD caused conductive non-PROTECTIVELY EARTHED ACCESSIBLE PARTS to exceed limits of 8.4, the cord anchorage shall be made of: insulating material, OR metal insulated from conductive ACCESSIBLE PARTS non-PROTECTIVELY EARTHED by a MEANS OF PROTECTION, OR metal provided with an insulating lining affixed to cord anchorage, except when it is a flexible bushing forming part of the cord guard in 8.11.3.6, and complying with the requirements for one MEANS OF PROTECTION.

For cord guard compliance per IEC 60335-1:2001 Clause 25.14: ME EQUIPMENT placed such that axis of cord guard projected at an angle of 45° with cord free from stress, and a mass equal 10 x D2 gram attached to the free end of cord (where D is the cord diameter). This test applies to POWER SUPPLY CORDS other than for STATIONARY ME EQUIPMENT.
